morbi.headline: Mixed margin pressures for Morbi ceramics as energy costs fluctuate amid weak exports.
what_changed: Industrial propane gas prices increased by ₹3 to ₹104/kg while natural gas prices received a ₹5 discount.
Ceramic exports to the Gulf resumed, though the general export outlook remains depressed.
Local manufacturers raised unresolved power, water, and infrastructure issues with state ministers.
stress_signals: Industrial propane gas hiked by ₹3 to ₹104/kg, inflating production costs [9e8c549b7c05]
Persistent infrastructural issues including power supply and water availability [8b17a473b62a]
Overall export demand for Morbi ceramic shipments remains weak despite Gulf trade resuming [c2b4a2f5422a]
Suspicious imported coal stock found in a closed ceramic factory in Rafaleshwar GIDC [f675c060fa53]
improvement_signals: Natural gas prices reduced by ₹5 from ₹82 following ministerial intervention [279312659941]
Kajaria Ceramics reported Q2 2026 sales and profit beats and invested ₹1.21 Cr in Sunsure Solar [83abd2d67eca, a2787358932e]
Ceramic export shipments to Gulf destinations have resumed [c2b4a2f5422a]
what_to_watch: Margin impact on unorganized tile units balancing higher propane costs against natural gas discounts.
Order book strength and receivables tracking for units dependent on Gulf export corridors.
Operational continuity and power stability metrics following ministerial representations.

surat.headline: Surat faces severe textile payment delays despite selective recoveries and policy support.
what_changed: Severe trade credit stretching in the weaving sub-segment with payment delays exceeding 200 days, leading to protests and police intervention.
Labor tensions resolved in the embroidery sub-sector via an agreement, while weavers face ongoing risk of fresh agitation.
Textile PLI scheme turnover threshold was halved and extended to FY 2033-34, easing eligibility criteria.
stress_signals: Weavers staged protests as outstanding textile payment dues exceeded 200 days ahead of Diwali [774ba602b06e].
Surat Mercantile Association highlighted a severe payment crisis threatening the survival of small textile traders [e0787797133b].
Trade payment recovery disputes between weavers and traders escalated to police intervention [80f44f3f370f] alongside allegations of withheld dues [9a8429b49c99].
Textile mills hit by power cuts and electricity tariff hikes, while US demand slowdown impacts apparel and diamond exporters [385f9b90ae46, caa34a6cf84e].
improvement_signals: Traders across Global, Bombay, and Ring Road markets recovered Rs 6 crore in stuck payments for 70 textile traders [a523a4bf860d].
Embroidery workers ended labor movement following a mutual agreement with unit owners [3a495ae0b3ee].
Government halved the PLI scheme turnover limit and extended the scheme up to FY 2033-34 [c7ee55f3effe].
what_to_watch: Working capital cycle metrics and receivables aging beyond 180 days across MSME weaving and trading accounts.
Potential fresh labor unrest and operational shutdowns across local man-made fabric manufacturing units.
Divergence in diamond sub-segment performance between export slowdown headwinds and pre-Diwali demand uptick.
Uptake of relaxed PLI scheme norms by local textile units for capital investment.
